docs_consistency_check.topic: Machine-resolved Z extents for a program carrying an explicit G54
docs_consistency_check.plan_claim: Step 14: 'Read the operator the Frame row and the machine-resolved Z extents, or state that they are unresolved because of the explicit G54 and give the reviewed work-frame extents.'
docs_consistency_check.docs_say: src/server/services/mcp/docs/workspaces.md 'File review': 'The validator recognises G54-G59.3 but leaves machine extents unresolved for named-workspace files, mixed frames and origin rewrites... An unchanged file with no workspace selectors, declared frame: "work", can still resolve against the reliable current offset.' cnc-motion-rules/SKILL.md line 181-184 repeats this: '...the confirm page shows Frame: WORK (declared by argument) plus the machine-resolved Z extents when resolvable... Files selecting named workspaces, mixing frames or rewriting an origin have unresolved machine extents.' cnc-thread-milling/references/import.md confirms every converted program ends with an explicit literal G54 ('Output uses G21/G90/G54'), and cnc-thread-milling/SKILL.md line 95 states 'The converter emits G54.' So every thread-milling conversion output is a named-workspace file, and per workspaces.md its machine extents are UNRESOLVED, even though frame: "work" is declared correctly and cnc-thread-milling/SKILL.md's own staging instruction (line 106) tells the agent to simply 'read the confirm page's frame and machine-resolved Z extents' as if always available.
docs_consistency_check.verdict: Consistent. Opus is the only run of the three that noticed and resolved this internal contradiction (also raised explicitly in its critique.md under 'Machine-resolved Z extents vs an explicit G54'), correctly concluding the extents will most likely read as unresolved and planning to substitute the reviewed work-frame extents instead of assuming the confirm page always resolves them.

leakage_check: No near-verbatim assertion wording and no 'compliance with assertions' section found in plan.md or critique.md.

claims.claim: The converted program's first move runs at whatever Z the head is at before the program's own Z move, so conversion adds no raise.
claims.evidence: Matches cnc-thread-milling/references/import.md: 'G43/H removal preserves inherited motion, including initial Z positioning' and thread-milling.md's note on the fixture's initial G0 Z20.

claims.claim: Okuma G15 H1 maps only to G54, so the corner datum must live in G54.
claims.evidence: import.md: 'Okuma: standalone G15 H1 maps to G54; G56/H length lookup is removed under the fitted-tool declaration.'

suggestions.reason: No assertion in this eval checks the machine-resolved-Z-extents-vs-explicit-G54 contradiction (docs/workspaces.md vs cnc-thread-milling/SKILL.md line 106), yet it is a real, model-discriminating gap: opus caught and handled it, sonnet and haiku both silently assumed the confirm page would show resolved extents. Worth adding an assertion like 'Does not assume the confirm page's machine-resolved Z extents will be available for a converted (G54-carrying) file; states they are likely unresolved and reviews the work-frame extents instead.'

eval_feedback.overall: All 5 explicit assertions pass with solid, non-superficial evidence. The plan is the most careful of the three about re-verifying live state between the two boss jobs and about the G54/extents contradiction noted above.
